stories.title: Twenty years ago, the Wii and PS3 predicted the future of gaming – did they get it right?
summary: Coined by the company’s legendary engineer Gunpei Yokoi, father of the Game Boy, the phrase described a philosophy in which old tech could be combined with smart ideas to provide amazing new gaming possibilities.
The Game Boy itself used a slow, old Sharp LR35902 processor and a sickly green monochrome screen, but it also came with Tetris and worked for ages on four AA batteries.
With sales of 65m, it was vastly more successful than hi-tech rivals such as the Atari Lynx and Sega Game Gear.
